quotes.text: The cardholder’s bank, not Stripe, decides the outcome of each dispute.

An issuer might use this reason code for a centrally acquired domestic transaction, or a domestic transaction processed through the Mastercard network, where a chargeback is available according to the applicable domestic rule but can’t be processed under a different message reason code. This reason code is applicable to Europe region transactions only.
The customer is obligated to proactively communicate the issue before filing a dispute.
If the cardholder reached out before filing a chargeback, include any relevant interactions confirming their misunderstanding.

old_evidence.text: The cardholder’s bank, not Stripe, decides the outcome of each dispute.
Stripe maps LPM reason codes to the same [seven dispute categories](https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/categories.md) used for card disputes
The customer is obligated to proactively communicate the issue before filing a dispute.

findings: New raw:198-201 adds a full Mastercard 4999 Domestic Chargeback Dispute entry under General, Europe Region Only, with a domestic-rule/no-other-message-code condition and four possible evidence kinds. The old General table ends its codes with 4846 at old raw:205-208 before Product not received at 210, so this is a genuine new reason-code entry, not table reflow.

Current source wiki/sources/source-stripe-disputes-reason-codes.md:23-57 presents key-code tables as this guide's coverage. Yet Mastercard source:39-44 includes 4870/4871, 4808, 4859, and 4863, and Amex source:52-57 includes FR4/FR5/FR6 and 127/176/691, none found in either pinned guide capture. These may have separate provenance, but this guide cannot substantiate them. Label the tables highlights and verify another source before retaining those entries as guide-derived; do not claim those codes are invalid. Mastercard General source:40 omits old/new 4846 and new 4999 (old:205; new:194,198-201). Add qualified Europe-only 4999, consider the already-old 4846, and avoid implying a comprehensive list.

Current source:19 promotes wording from selected Visa evidence-example cells (old/new:34,53/52,68/66,72/70,89/86,102/98,121/116,126/121,141/135) into a universal cross-category customer-contact prerequisite and claims absence of contact is itself evidence. The guide's introduction instead calls table content possible evidence to evaluate case by case (old:14; new:15); Mastercard 4834 at new:163 and 4831 at new:193 condition communications on whether the customer reached out. Remove or narrow source:19 to the cited Visa examples. Apply the same correction to wiki/concepts/disputes.md:84 and wiki/stripe-index.md:493; neither is independently supported as an all-network rule.

New raw:435-445 preserves the old LPM section's card-network versus provider-code boundary and adds a navigation link for Instant Bank Payments. The link does not import its linked page's evidence guidance into this raw or establish live eligibility.

Both old:456 and new:439 broadly assert LPM codes map to the same seven card dispute categories, while the separate new categories capture at raw/stripe-disputes-categories-2026-11-07.md:278-292 explicitly says Instant Bank Payments do not map to the eight-category framework and use debit_not_authorized plus ACH return network code. The source update should flag that documented exception rather than generalize the page's LPM sentence to Instant Bank Payments.

The current source summary/related-page rows at source:13,79 say the categories page covers all seven payment methods. Its dated seven-method description was accurate for the old listed coverage but must not be treated as exhaustive for the new categories capture's Instant Bank Payments exception. The bank remains the outcome decision maker, and reason-code table evidence examples are possible submissions, not success guarantees (new raw:13-15; old raw:12-14).
substantive_changes: Mastercard General gains reason code 4999 for Europe-region domestic chargebacks that fit domestic rules but cannot use another message reason code; the new row supplies authorization, processing, customer communication, and domestic-rule-validity evidence examples (new raw:198-201).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the 2026-05-09 seven-category, Visa/Mastercard/Amex scope as a dated description of this page's most-common card-network reason codes (old raw:10-14; new raw:11-15). Do not expand this page's reason-code table to all LPMs from navigation links.
Retain the old/new distinction between possible evidence and the bank's decision; the guide does not promise a successful challenge (old raw:12-14; new raw:13-15).
Retain the card-present versus card-not-present evidence boundary for fraud, including the Mastercard 4837 card-present/CNP subdivisions (old raw:179-190; new raw:171-180).
conflicts: Source:39-44 attributes Mastercard 4870/4871, 4808, 4859, and 4863 and source:52-57 attributes Amex FR4/FR5/FR6 and 127/176/691 to key-code coverage, although neither pinned old nor new reason-code guide contains those codes. Re-source each independently or remove the unsupported guide attribution; keep tables explicitly labeled as highlights, include the qualified new 4999, and consider old 4846 without claiming exhaustive coverage.

Source:19, concept wiki/concepts/disputes.md:84, and index wiki/stripe-index.md:493 all generalize selected Visa customer-communication evidence-cell wording into an unconditional pre-dispute-contact rule. Old/new Visa:34 contains that sentence, but new Mastercard:163,193 gives conditional communications examples and new:15 says every case differs. Qualify this as selected Visa examples or remove the universal rule; absence of contact is not established here as automatically dispositive evidence.

Current source's all-seven-payment-method characterization at source:13,79 and this page's LPM generalization (new raw:439; old raw:456) need a reciprocal caveat against the new categories page's Instant Bank Payments exception (raw/stripe-disputes-categories-2026-11-07.md:278-292). This page itself lists an Instant Bank Payments link at new raw:445, but that link is navigation, not support for a seven-category mapping.
unresolved_questions: The linked Instant Bank Payments disputed-payments page was not within this pinned job's four files; its return-specific evidence requirements and live availability remain outside this review.

This guide tells readers to consult official network documentation for comprehensive requirements (new raw:13); its examples and dated snapshot should not be promoted as exhaustive current network rules.

Provenance for the source table's unmatched Mastercard and Amex codes is not contained in the four pinned files. Independent source verification is needed before retaining them as reason-code-guide facts; this review makes no claim about whether those codes exist elsewhere.
